title: Secrets of Strixhaven Promos: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: By himself, Lluwen couldn't have hoped to calm the Dawning Archaic—but any time it really mattered, he was never alone.
Raising spirits is easier than taming them.
"Our lives are built upon our pasts. What happens, then, if we are cut off from them?" —Augusta, dean of order
"My inklings are ideal for gathering information. There's no place on Arcavios they can't reach."
Though not all her students have wings, she's determined to help them reach new heights.
"Dangerously overflowing with creative expression." —*Strixhaven Star* gallery show review
The harder a foe strikes, the stronger a Dragonsguard's defenses become.
"Theory? Meet practice." —Tam, Quandrix second-year
"To the patient mind, no problem is unsolvable."
"If you take the time to listen, the archaics will tell you that this world has been torn asunder and remade many times before." —Jadzi, Oracle of Arcavios
The darkest corners of the Detention Bog hide natural laboratories that quietly spawn deadly infections.
In the wake of the archaics' rampage, much worse was to come.
Although lumarets are small magical creatures, they can gather to eliminate larger threats.
Quintorius found that every new discovery motivated him to keep exploring.
"My media? Fury and flame."
In the grief that followed the Invasion, Willowdusk's office turned into an unofficial hideaway for overwhelmed students.
"All growth comes at a cost. It's up to each of us to determine if the result is worth the sacrifice." —Oracle Jadzi, to Tam
"Yes, she is blocking the path. Are you volunteering to move her?" —Tam, to Kirol
"I know the prompt was to replicate a scurrid, but I took some creative liberties with my version."
Few relics survived the turmoil of the Blood Age; those that did are powerful, dangerous, or both.
"Good play, team! Now let's run it again until it's perfect!"
Despite Blex's passing, Witherbloom students still continued the tradition of a yearly search in his honor. His son, however, took little effort to find.
In the gloomy depths of Widdershins Hall sits an iron belly—always hungry, but generous to those who feed it.
Prismari students are never afraid to let their imaginations run wild.
"By all means, let's debate."
"This last step is very important. You'll need to know if the friend you're searching for is alive or dead."
Two tired souls finally found something to unite them.
"Creatures that have survived blood-soaked millennia should not be underestimated." —Nev, dean of substance
"Do you think I've spent a lifetime studying war and learned nothing?"
"What the mind conceives," began Dean Adrix. "Magic can achieve," assured Dean Nev.
The archaics experience all of Arcavian history. Changing that fate threatens their very existence.
School styluses are just tools. Passion is a Prismari's true instrument.
As the marvels of living art they are, elemental whales can't resist contributing to Summitfest's displays.
"Knowledge is your armor. Use it wisely, and it will keep you safe." —Augusta, dean of order
"The *artist* should suffer for their craft, not the audience!" —Galazeth Prismari
So intense was their hatred they didn't realize how lonely they'd become. In the end, all they had was each other, and they hated that, too.
"Leave everything on the stage and give them a performance they'll never forget."
"Life is defined by change. When I shucked my flesh to combat the Phyrexian infection, it was not loss to me, merely a new state of being." —Moseo, dean of the vein
"Nature is chaos governed by principle. In analyzing these patterns, I hope to protect Strixhaven's future from any more tragedy." —Adrix, dean of theory
"The most cordial words are often the ones intended to deceive. It's only of late that I've realized how much strength honesty requires." —Embrose, dean of shadow
"Careful ideation crashes together with wild creativity. Though I am grateful to be made dean, I've found it difficult to represent just the one side." —Veyran, dean of perfection
"Study of the past is preparation for the future. My fail-safe spell, activated upon my death, was precaution born from tales of the careless." —Augusta, dean of order
